title: SDK Observability and Telemetry Cookbook for Client Integrations
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This cookbook provides concrete, copy-pasteable guidance for instrumenting Redwood SDK clients (all official language SDKs) with telemetry and observability signals that are compatible with our platform dashboards and SLOs. It focuses on three goals:

- Make failures diagnosable quickly by on-call engineers.
- Ensure cost and latency metrics are available at token/route/model granularity.
- Keep client-side telemetry low-overhead and privacy-conscious.

Audience:
- SDK authors and maintainers
- Integrations engineers and partner SDKs
- Solutions engineers helping customers instrument clients

Key signals (what we collect and why):

1) Request lifecycle events (traceable per request)
- request.start — when the SDK begins network work
- request.end — on successful completion
- request.error — on final failure
Purpose: Build traces across client -> Redwood gateway -> serving runtime for latency breakdowns and root-cause analysis.

2) Token & response metrics
- tokens.prompt, tokens.completion (counts)
- bytes_sent, bytes_received
Purpose: Chargeback, cost attribution, and anomaly detection for sudden token spikes.

3) Model variant & config metadata
- model_id, model_variant, quantization_profile, max_tokens, temperature
Purpose: Link client calls to model performance profiles and audit regressions after rollouts.

4) Sampling of interactions for quality monitoring
- hashed-session-id, prompt-hash, response-hash (not raw text)
Purpose: Allow fuzzed sampling for evals and guardrails while preserving PII constraints.

Instrumentation patterns (recommended):

- Minimal synchronous hooks: provide blocking hooks that fire before the network call and after the response/error. Keep payloads small (IDs, counts, timings).
- Async background uploads: aggregate and upload telemetry in batches (default 30s or 250 events, whichever comes first).
- Respect user privacy: do not send raw prompt or response text unless explicitly enabled via an opt-in API and flagged in the payload.
- Pluggable exporters: SDKs should support exporters for OTLP, Prometheus pushgateway, and our internal collector.

Standard fields (common schema):
- trace_id: unique 64-bit hex string
- span_id: unique 64-bit hex string
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601 string
- route: SDK route name (e.g., text.generate, chat.complete)
- model_id: canonical model id (e.g., redwood/gptx-8k)
- latency_ms: integer
- status: ok | error | aborted
- error_code: short string when status != ok
- tokens_prompt: integer
- tokens_completion: integer

NOTE: All fields must be top-level and use snake_case to match our ingestion schemas.

Quickstart examples (JavaScript):

1) Synchronous hook instrumentation (copy into your SDK client class):

const telem = require('@redwood/telem');

class RedwoodClient {
  async call(route, payload) {
    const start = Date.now();
    const traceId = telem.newTraceId();
    telem.emit('request.start', { trace_id: traceId, route });
    try {
      const res = await this._http.post(`/v1/${route}`, payload);
      const latency = Date.now() - start;
      telem.emit('request.end', { trace_id: traceId, route, latency_ms: latency, status: 'ok' });
      return res.data;
    } catch (err) {
      const latency = Date.now() - start;
      telem.emit('request.error', { trace_id: traceId, route, latency_ms: latency, status: 'error', error_code: err.code || 'network_error' });
      throw err;
    }
  }
}

2) Background batching exporter (Node):

const batch = new Map();
setInterval(() => {
  const payload = Array.from(batch.values());
  if (payload.length) sendToCollector(payload).then(() => batch.clear());
}, 30000);

function enqueue(event) {
  const key = `${event.trace_id}:${event.route}:${event.timestamp_utc}`;
  batch.set(key, event);
}

Configuration table (recommended defaults):

| config_key | default | notes |
|------------|---------|-------|
| telemetry.enabled | true | Master switch to disable all SDK telemetry |
| telemetry.exporter | "internal_otlp" | Options: internal_otlp, otlp, prometheus, noop |
| telemetry.batch_size | "250" | Number of events before flush |
| telemetry.batch_interval_ms | "30000" | Max interval before flush |
| telemetry.sample_rate | "0.05" | Fraction of requests to full-sample for quality (0-1) |
| telemetry.anonymize_hash_salt | "<app-salt>" | Salt to produce non-reversible hashed ids |

Privacy and consent patterns:

1) Explicit opt-in for raw payload capture
- API: client.enableRawCapture({purpose: 'eval', reason: 'customer_agreement_123'})
- Persist an audit log locally and include consent metadata in telemetry uploads.

2) Hash-only sampling for QA
- Only send prompt-hash and response-hash unless raw capture is enabled. Use HMAC-SHA256 with anonymize_hash_salt.

3) Data retention override
- Provide client API to request early deletion of queued telemetry for a session id. Honor deletion requests within 24 hours.

On-call playbook snippets (for SRE/DevEx):

1) Investigating a spike in tokens across customers:
1. Check platform ingestion dashboard: tokens.total by model_id over last 15m
2. Filter by route and customer_id; check sdk.client_version tag
3. If token-per-request has increased, correlate with rollout timestamps (redwood/rollouts)
4. If instrumentation shows higher sample_rate, verify SDK config pushed from customer environment

2) High 5xx rate from SDK clients:
1. Confirm client-side latency distribution and network error codes via traces
2. Ask customer to upgrade to SDK version >= 3.4.1 which includes retry/timeouts fixes
3. If still failing, collect a sanitized trace bundle (trace ids + route + timestamps + response status) following privacy rules

Edge cases and defensive checks:

- Backpressure: if the exporter queue grows beyond 5k events, drop oldest events and emit internal metric telemetry.dropped_events with reason "queue_full".
- Boot-time safety: disable blocking disk writes during SDK init; keep recovery async with exponential backoff (base 200ms, max 60s).
- Clock skew: if timestamp skew > 5 minutes from server, include client_time_offset_ms in payload for debugging.

Compatibility and SDK author checklist:

- [ ] Implements standard fields schema and snake_case keys
- [ ] Exposes telemetry.enabled and telemetry.exporter options in constructor
- [ ] Uses hashed session ids, not raw IDs, in telemetry by default
- [ ] Provides a clear opt-in for raw payload capture with audit logging
- [ ] Implements background batching with configurable size and interval
- [ ] Provides unit tests for exporter failure handling and queue eviction
- [ ] Includes a docs page linking to platform ingestion schema and sample dashboards

Appendix: Example OTLP-style JSON event (sanitized):

  "trace_id": "a3f4b2c9d8e7f001",

  "status": "ok",
